items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you also recorded with Mez Mezro and his orchestra

ctx.x: Well, whatever he thought, I think he had much more to say, and he should have continued.

Then, now we return to that Chocolate Dandies date we mentioned in October of 1933, which was the first recordings with Teddy Wilson, and then a few days later . . . that was a smaller group of some members of your band and some white musicians, namely, Max Kominski [phonetic] and Floyd O’Brien [phonetic] and, reputedly, Mez Mezro [phonetic] banging on the drums somewhere, but that’s not confirmed. But, do you remember, was this another idea of John Hammond, to sort of have an integrated recording unit?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: No, that's what I might call an interesting anecdote, but I don't remember it.

ctx.x: : Then he says that he stalled off the people that were leaving him and they got Benny Carter instead. To do arrangements. He says, "I was ready to quit, and as they started out for the McKenzie-Hagen rehearsals soon after, Max Kaminsky and Bud Freeman told me not to worry; that the band was no good anyway." This rival band, you see.
Then he says, " They told me we've been rehearsing some Carter -- one Carter arrangement, the first 8 bars only, and we can't even get it out yet!"

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Mezzrow... mentions that you helped him with what he calls the first interracial band

ctx.x: Another thing, around that time. There's a -- in a discussion with Bud Freeman, that was not Bud Freeman, although he was involved -- it was Mezz Mezzrow, Mezzra -- Mezzra, in his book, 'Really the BLues' mentions that you helped him with what he calls the first interracial band; everybody's got the first interracial band -- he had it in 1933.
He says in August of 1933 he signed a contract with a financial backer to support a mixed Big Band, which had Alex Hill, as the arranger, to front it. This is in Mezzrow's Mezra's book.
